name: Ban'ethil Barrow Den
summary: Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun Ban'ethil Barrow Den beneath Teldrassil's roots. The sacred chambers were made for the sleeping Druids of the Talon, whose spirits commune with the Emerald Dream. Now the den is a dangerous warren, and the druids within are at risk.

sections.title: A Defiled Sanctuary
sections.body: Ban'ethil Barrow Den lies beneath Teldrassil's roots, with upper and lower chambers. Barrow dens shelter night elf druids as they sleep and send their spirits into the Emerald Dream. This den was made for the Druids of the Talon to commune with nature. Its halls once held quiet meditation, but the corruption spreading through Teldrassil's wildlife reached the Gnarlpine furbolgs. They invaded the den and made its hollowed chambers a fortified warren.

sections.title: The Gnarlpine Incursion
sections.body: The Gnarlpine tribe has gone mad under a mysterious corruption spreading across the World Tree. Its furbolgs drove out or endangered the sleeping druids, and now guard the winding tunnels fiercely, attacking any night elf who approaches. Teldrassil's defenders must drive them back to protect the vulnerable druids and the sacred relics trapped in the den's lower depths.

faq.answer: Ban'ethil Barrow Den is a hollow beneath Teldrassil, made by night elves to shelter the sleeping Druids of the Talon. Their spirits roam the Emerald Dream while they sleep.

faq.q: Why are there furbolgs inside Ban'ethil Barrow Den?
faq.answer: The Gnarlpine furbolgs fell to a spreading corruption among Teldrassil's creatures. They turned hostile, invaded the den, displaced its keepers, and threaten the sleeping druids.

faq.q: What are the sections of the barrow den?
faq.answer: The den has two connected tiers, the Upper Den near the entrance passages and the Lower Den deeper among the subterranean roots.

faq.q: Why are barrow dens so important to druids?
aliases: why do druids sleep in barrows
faq.answer: Barrow dens shelter druids whose deep sleep lets their consciousness enter the Emerald Dream. Their waking bodies lie helpless for years or decades, so they need safe, secure shelter.

angles.text: As a druid, you can see Ban'ethil as sacred ground for the Cenarion Circle, built to protect the Druids of the Talon as they commune with the Emerald Dream.
As a night elf, you can see the Gnarlpine occupation of Ban'ethil as a warning of the sickness spreading through your new home, Teldrassil.
